display.title: Treasure Island: A Mashal About Freedom and Mitzvos
display.summary_short: What true freedom means after Pesach, why we count the Omer, and a parable of a shipwrecked man made king of an island who forgets to send its treasures home.
display.summary_long: Coming from Pesach, the time of our freedom, the storyteller asks what freedom really is. A flower is free when it stays rooted, a cow when it can roam, a pianist when he can play; a Jew is free when he can do the mitzvos he was created for. That is why the Exodus leads to Matan Torah, and why the Jews counted the days, climbing out of the impurity of Egypt one level at a time, as we do in Sefiras HaOmer, now in the week of Gevurah. He then tells a mashal he heard from his father: Yisroel, the only survivor of a shipwreck, is crowned king of an island and spends its treasures on towers, parks and paved streets. One day another castaway arrives, Yisroel is sent home in his old rags, and the guard will not let him near the treasury. He realizes he should have sent the riches home while he could. The lesson: this world is the treasure island, and every mitzvah, even eating and sleeping for the sake of Heaven, is treasure stored up for the days of Moshiach.
display.lesson: Use every moment in this world to gather mitzvos and Torah, because they are the treasures we keep forever. True freedom is doing what Hashem created us for.
